content:
maria: Deploy canary of cuToolkit 12 images to eu-west-1 finished, but we're seeing host driver/RTLD errors on older nodes. Logs: ```Container init: error while loading shared libraries: libnvidia-ptx.so: invalid ELF header
modprobe nvidia: FATAL: Module compiled with different gcc/abi
nvidia-smi: Driver/library mismatch```
ajay: Oof. Which nodes are affected? kernel versions?
maria: Affected fleet: g4dn-type nodes in eu-west-1 and a handful in us-east-1. uname -a shows 5.4.0-116-generic on the failing ones.
kevin: Sounds like module ABI mismatch after host driver stayed at 510 while toolkit images expect 535. Did we mix driver rollouts with toolkit rollout?
maria: We only rolled image bundles (container/toolkit) — host driver didn't get updated. The containers ship PTX compiled for 535 and the kernel rejects the module. Some containers dropped to fail loop, causing pods to restart and kube-scheduler to pack others onto fewer nodes.
olga: Are these nodes pinned (nodeSelector) for certain customers? We might be over-scheduling because pinned workloads couldn't be placed and kept retrying.
ajay: Confirmed: two customer pools are nodeAffinity:pinned to g4dn-type. When pods crash they keep rescheduling until backoff; that pressure spilled into non-pinned pools.
maria: Quick mitigation: rolled back container image tag to cu11-compatible image for the pinned nodepool. Deploy-bot: rollback triggered by maria (INF-2345)
deploy-bot: rollback job created: job/rollback-cu11-1768500000 — status: in_progress
kevin: Ops: we should also cordon the old kernel hosts and schedule maintenance to update host drivers, or mark them for retirement if they're EOL.
olga: We can't update drivers easily in eu-west due to maintenance windows for customers. Consider adding a runtime fallback in image: if driver < 535 then set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= and run a soft-fallback path or start a lightweight shim.
ajay: Practical short-term: k8s taint the failing nodes so scheduler stops placing new pods, drain the worst offenders, and scale up a temporary pool (spot vs reserved?) to absorb load. Cost note: spinning-on-demand a100s would be $$$; prefer reserving cheaper g5/odes if compatible.
maria: Drains started: node/g4dn-23 cordoned, drain in progress. Also uploading a patched image with LD_LIBRARY_PATH override to prefer container's libnvidia and a fallback entrypoint script. Testing now.
ops-runner: SRE alert: NCCL fatal errors spiked 4x in last 20m, new job failures ~120 -> blocking inference backfills.
kevin: If NCCL fails because of mismatched kernel modules, nothing we do at container level will fix inter-node comms. We need host-side driver parity or force single-node scheduling for sensitive jobs.
olga: Proposal: update rollout plan to include driver daemonset that handles driver upgrades in waves, with canary in us-west-2 only, and explicit drain/restore hooks. Document in INF runbook.
maria: Agreed. Creating INF-2346 runbook draft. For immediate: rollback completed for pinned pools, error rate dropped ~70%.
ajay: Next steps: 1) freeze toolkit images for pinned pools, 2) plan driver upgrade windows, 3) implement node labelling to avoid mixed-driver clusters, 4) schedule capacity increase for next 48h to reduce retries.
kevin: Also add a postmortem with cost impact: extra 6 hours of burst capacity and manual ops time ~10 engineer-hours. Estimate bill ~$9k for the event. Put on the weekly incident review.
maria: Thanks. I'll follow up with PR for the rollback images and link to INF-2346. :thumbsup:
